title: The Nature of Virtue and its Fruits
english: Ten years have not passed, and the impassibility of the wise man is because he aims to prepare [the soul] as it is suitable for the marriage. The matters of the upbringing have already been spoken of, that according to the aim of virtue, it is necessary to have first used the introductory things, so that through them he might first become a parent; and the children from the preliminary training are no less children of virtue because of the aim having done the same toward it. Having used this, therefore, he accomplished a better acquisition; for progress is most ready for the wise man.

"And he saw that she had conceived in the womb, and the lady was dishonored in her presence" (Gen 18:13). The aim, as has been spoken, is for the wise man to be trained in the preliminary training and in the shadow, so that having been trained in these things, he may proceed to the greater things; for as such a sequence is proper, so there is not a following return from the knowledge of the perfects into the smaller things. For the apostle neglects, writing to the Galatians, those who wish to live with the shadow of the law after the gospel (Gal 4:25). For the Jews, having the shadow as a companion, [are one thing], and the Galatians, after believing the gospel, wished to Judaize (Acts 15:5), having been deceived by a certain Ebion, who wished to Judaize after Christianizing and was persuading the others thus, since he had the epithet of this name among the apostles because of his making poverty manifest; for Ebion is interpreted as poor, because of his shallow and poor intellect, being called Ebion the poor; for that the Galatians were Greeks, Paul writes: "But at that time you did not know God, but served those which are by nature not gods; but now having known God, or rather having been known by God" (Gal 4:8). He therefore blames them, as has been said; for it is necessary to repay the promise of the Scriptures: "Having begun in the Spirit, are you now being perfected in the flesh?" (Gal 3:3); for having once been cast into a divine beginning, they were not appropriately seeking the types, for they were seeking them at an unseasonable time. For it is necessary to understand for what reason the sensory circumcision is given and until when...

For what period must he live as a citizen? If someone perceives this, he has fathered a child from a concubine, and after this he is able to perceive the circumcision being made in the heart by the Spirit (Rom 2:29). And this holy man, following the guidance of virtue, entered toward her to whom a maidservant had been handed to him, as we have shown, who also conceived, toward whom it is not fitting to remain thereafter exceeding what is necessary.

For many, having used preliminary exercises for the sake of complete instruction, having left behind them such things, are born in a slave-like manner and in a certain way dishonor virtue. But these things must not be referred to the person of Abraham, but to such a manner of those using this kind of way. And if, since we said that virtue... is the thing presupposing the things of the introduction, someone says that the offspring are a kind of part of it and such a person dwells with virtue primarily—for the underlying subject acts according to its postulates—it must be said therefore that of those things happening in time, some are prior to some and others are later, but when they are simultaneous, we take as understood that of those existing at once, one precedes and the other follows, as if regarding natural causes; virtue indeed is the cause of all things happening through it; therefore, even if such things precede it in time, it is by nature prior, just as marriage exists prior to child-rearing; for because of these things marriage... of virtue. And regarding the other sciences, the same...

Therefore, he who prefers other things to virtue dishonors virtue; for if someone were to choose it not for its own sake but for the sake of some other praise or glory, he in a certain way dishonors the good, it not receiving dishonor in itself. And take note that it has not even been said that Abram dishonored it—for this would not be harmonious with him—but since it is possible [to happen] from...
